sample_unit: evaluations (50 questions x 6 models x 3 repetitions)

links.outcome: Accuracy and hallucination rate with vs without guideline retrieval grounding
links.effect: Content-level hallucination fell from 42% to 4%; judge accuracy rose by pooled +0.64 points (95% CI 0.47-0.80); citation groundedness rose from 0% to 51-89%.
links.quote: On the judge, content-level hallucination fell from 42% to 4% and accuracy rose by a pooled +0.64 points (95% CI 0.47-0.80); the accuracy gain persisted after adjustment for response length (+0.48, 95% CI 0.22-0.73), which retrieval shortened rather than lengthened.

links.outcome: Retrieval recall and citation groundedness of a documented guideline RAG corpus
links.effect: Retrieval recall@5 was 92%; citation groundedness rose from 0% to 51-89% deterministically from retrieval logs.
links.quote: Deterministically from the retrieval logs, citation groundedness rose from 0% to 51-89% and retrieval recall@5 was 92%.

links.outcome: Citation groundedness and auditability of answers with guideline retrieval
links.effect: Citation groundedness rose from 0% to 51-89%; hallucination and auditability gains were consistent across all models.
links.quote: The accuracy gain was large for weaker base models and small or non-significant for already-strong ones, whereas the hallucination and auditability gains were consistent across all models.

links.outcome: Hallucination rate of standard LLMs without guideline access
links.effect: Content-level hallucination was 42% without retrieval, falling to 4% with retrieval; residual hallucination requires human oversight.
links.quote: On the judge, content-level hallucination fell from 42% to 4% and accuracy rose by a pooled +0.64 points (95% CI 0.47-0.80); the accuracy gain persisted after adjustment for response length (+0.48, 95% CI 0.22-0.73), which retrieval shortened rather than lengthened.

unlisted_practices: Rater-independent evaluation measures (deterministic log metrics, condition-blind LLM judge) because RAG answers are recognizable to blinded experts

screen.practice: retrieval grounding added to an existing tool
screen.reason: Evaluates LLMs answering clinical guideline questions in a paired within-model benchmark directly testing the impact of adding retrieval-augmented generation (RAG guideline grounding) on safety, hallucination, and accuracy.
